Topsoil, Overburden and Coal Removal
The topsoil is removed with motorized scrapers and is initially stockpiled. When sufficient spoils have been graded, topsoil thus stripped is redistributed directly on the graded spoils. Overburden is drilled with electric-powered, track-mounted rotary drills. The drills can cut 9 to 15-inch diameter holes, producing blastholes whose pattern and spacing are dictated by the physical characteristics of the overburden material. The holes are loaded with appropriate detonators and an explosive consisting of 94 percent ammonium nitrate and 6 percent fuel oil. The explosive charges are then detonated in a predetermined fashion designed both to efficiently fragment the rock and to minimize damaging ground vibrations. A large (75-cubic-yard capacity or bigger) walking dragline then removes the broken overburden above the uppermost coal bed and places this material into previously mined areas.
The top of the coal is cleaned by a bulldozer. Then the coal is drilled, blasted, and loaded into 110-ton capacity bottom-dump trucks by large front-end loaders.
Lower beds are mined in the same way, beginning with drilling the interburden. Where multiple seams are being mined, a long pit is needed to maintain a good separation between the stages of overburden and coal removal for safe, efficient operation.
